docs.summary: The CPU-baked physics representation of a [`Mesh`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Resources.Mesh): the triangle soup (mesh-local space) plus a Jitter [`TriangleMesh`](#api~Prowl.Vector.Geometry.GeometryData.TriangleMesh) (the concave acceleration structure). Built once per mesh via [`BakeMesh`](#api~Prowl.Photonic.BakeMesh) and shared by every collider that uses the mesh, so the (potentially expensive) bake happens a single time instead of per MeshCollider instance.
The triangle soup in mesh-local space. Used to build convex hulls.

The concave triangle mesh, shareable across many `TriangleShape`s. It holds only the non-degenerate triangles, so it can contain fewer than [`Triangles`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.BakedPhysicsMesh~Triangles); index into it by its own `Indices.Length`, never by the soup count.
The [`Version`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Resources.Mesh~Version) this was baked from, used to detect staleness.

Bake a mesh into its physics representation. This is pure CPU work (it touches no GPU or main-thread-only state), so it is safe to call from any thread. Prefer [`BakeMesh`](#api~Prowl.Photonic.BakeMesh), which caches and shares the result per mesh.
